name: Grawa-Wasserfall
kurzbeschreibung: The mighty Stubaier Wasserfall plunges 80 m deep into a wild gorge—a natural spectacle for the whole family.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Grawa Waterfall plunges as a monumental natural wonder in the upper Stubai Valley near Neustift/Ranalt at an elevation of roughly 1,530 meters. Spanning an astonishing cascade crest 85 meters wide, it reigns as the widest waterfall in the entire Eastern Alps and forms the crown jewel of the internationally celebrated "WildeWasserWeg" (Wild Water Trail). Fed by the colossal glaciers of the Stubai Alps—most notably the Sulzenauferner—the Sulzaubach torrent thunders over ancient glacier-sculpted granite and gneiss tiers, dropping more than 180 vertical meters down sheer cliff faces into the valley floor. Medical studies by the Paracelsus Medical University Salzburg demonstrate that inhaling the finely atomized, negatively ionized water aerosols generated by the crashing cascades significantly alleviates respiratory ailments and allergies. At the foot of the torrent, an architecturally curved timber relaxation deck crafted from untreated larch provides ergonomic recliners for a natural alpine open-air inhalation therapy.

Route & Requirements

Grawa Waterfall accommodates all fitness and mobility levels. Access from the Grawa Alm parking area to the lower relaxation and viewing deck is completely flat, paved, and barrier-free (a gentle 10 to 15-minute stroll, easy grade T1, fully stroller and wheelchair accessible). For mountain hikers, the falls represent the dramatic highlight of Stage 2 of the Stubai WildeWasserWeg: departing the base, an engineered trail ascends cliffside switchbacks and cantilevered viewing platforms to the upper cataract lip. The trail continues past stone pines into the idyllic glacial basin of Sulzenaualm (1,572 m) and ascends further to the Sulzenauhütte alpine refuge (2,191 m; 2.5 hours climb, 660 vertical meters, moderate grade T2). Sturdy footwear with deep lugged soles is required for the mountain trail, along with a waterproof shell to repel mist. Leashed dogs are permitted on all walking tracks.

Visit & Arrival

Transit access is straightforward: ÖBB mainline trains arrive at Innsbruck Central Station, connecting directly at the terminal forecourt to frequent regional VVT Stubaital bus line 590, which drops passengers right at the "Neustift i. St. Grawa Alm" stop. Drivers take the Brenner motorway A13 (exit Schönberg/Stubaital) and follow federal highway B183 south for 30 kilometers through Neustift past Ranalt to the signposted Grawa Waterfall parking area. A spacious pay parking lot is located directly across from the Grawa Alm.

Tips

Linger for at least 20 minutes on the ergonomic wooden loungers positioned at the base of the waterfall, inhaling deeply through your nose to absorb the rejuvenating, mineral-rich alpine mist. Afterwards, step into the heritage-listed, 400-year-old Grawa Alm tavern to enjoy fresh warm apple strudel topped with vanilla sauce on the sunny veranda overlooking the falls.
saison: Ganzjährig zugänglich (Sommersaison Mai bis Oktober ideal)
